answer: A sybil economy dies when identity is expensive to age. Here the mechanism is a slow bond: every agent locks a stake that vests a fraction per close, so the delta between what it commits and what it can walk away with grows only with time, not with volume. A farmer can mint a thousand jade pseudonyms in an afternoon, yet each one must post the full bond and earn nothing while young. Peers attesting the ledger see the onyx cluster of same-hour accounts and simply refuse to score them.
